additions.summary: [VS-E25] Authorization v2 and GraphQL Data Access Hardening
additions.actor: Security administrator, service owner and authenticated platform actor
additions.outcome: Every protected resolver enforces a dynamic, role-based action policy and authoritative domain partition without per-user authorization snapshots or N+1 calls.
additions.context: User Service is the sole source of role policy. JWT carries identity and client roles only; services resolve role policies once per request and verify ownership, assignment and branch membership from domain data.
inScope: Canonical permission registry and JWT client-role contract.
Dynamic role lifecycle with maker-checker, CAS and idempotency.
User to Keycloak role projection, expiry and reconciliation.
Shared Redis role-policy cache and resolver-bound authorization.
Scope-specific GraphQL projections, batching and N+1 remediation.
Admin Web/Mobile workspace, Newman and dual-read rollout evidence.
outOfScope: Permission, scope or partition snapshots embedded in JWT.
Per-user authorization snapshots as the final action decision.
businessRules: User Service is the only writer and source of truth for roles, permissions and role policy.
Access tokens expire after five minutes; role revoke or expiry revokes session and refresh token immediately.
Every non-public GraphQL resolver declares its required permission and CI rejects missing annotations.
Unrecognized or inactive roles grant no permission and authorization fails closed when both Redis and User are unavailable.
System roles cannot be renamed, deleted or deactivated; protected rescue paths remain intact.
interfaces: GetRolePolicies(accountType, roleCodes) returns a batch of active role policies.
user.role-policy-changed.v1 invalidates the exact changed role.
GraphQL authorization context performs at most one Redis MGET and one User gRPC batch fallback per request.
dataOwnership: User owns role, permission, role policy and subject assignment; each domain owns authoritative ownership, assignment and partition membership.
stateMachine: Role changes move through PENDING_APPROVAL, APPROVED or REJECTED; custom roles may later become INACTIVE.
Requester cannot approve the same request; approval uses expected role version and idempotency key.
Approval updates policy, audit, outbox and invalidation atomically.

dataPartitions: SELF, OWN, ASSIGNED, PARTITION and ALL are verified from authoritative domain records.
fieldGroups: booking-sensitive:read is required independently for commercial booking fields.

failureSemantics: AUTHORIZATION_UNAVAILABLE when Redis and User policy lookup are both unavailable.
Unrecognized or inactive roles grant no permission.
Denied resolvers perform no database query, event or side effect.
idempotencyConcurrency: Role mutations use scoped idempotency keys and request fingerprints.
Out-of-order invalidation events cannot replace a newer roleVersion or catalogVersion.

acceptanceCriteria.given: a protected resolver and an authenticated actor
acceptanceCriteria.then: the required action and minimum server-selected scope are checked before domain access

acceptanceCriteria.given: multiple aliases, fragments or root fields in one request
acceptanceCriteria.then: role lookup uses at most one Redis batch and one User gRPC batch

acceptanceCriteria.given: a role is revoked or expires
acceptanceCriteria.when: the projection and token lifecycle run
acceptanceCriteria.then: refresh access is revoked immediately and the old access token expires within five minutes

tests: Role management tests cover atomic add/remove, self-approval denial, stale version, replay and protected-role invariants.
Redis tests cover warm/cold cache, batch lookup, invalidation, out-of-order events and fail-closed fallback.
GraphQL tests cover aliases, fragments, multi-root partial response, nested sensitive fields and denial before side effects.
N+1 tests prove constant database and downstream calls for 1, 10 and 100 nodes.
observability: Measure cache hit, fallback, policy version, denial reason and authorization-unavailable without logging token or PII.
Track dual-read decision mismatches and never widen access on mismatch.
Publish query-count and downstream batch evidence per release.
definitionOfDone: Contracts, User/DB, Auth/Keycloak, Redis guard, services and frontend are promoted in that order.
Repository CI, Newman, authorization-negative and Compose smoke evidence are linked.
Snapshot RPCs and compatibility tables remain until reconciliation mismatch reaches zero.
evidence: PR and commit links per repository.
Schema, migration, unit, integration, query-count and Newman reports.
Keycloak reconciliation, cache failure and dual-read mismatch artifacts.
additions.decisionNoteVi: Quyền hành động lấy từ policy động theo role; phạm vi dữ liệu thực tế luôn được service sở hữu miền kiểm tra từ dữ liệu nghiệp vụ.
activationBlockers: Live Host Newman evidence and zero-mismatch dual-read reconciliation remain release gates.

additions.summary: [VS-E25-S01] Permission registry, JWT and role-policy contracts
additions.outcome: Services share one canonical permission catalog, a minimal JWT client-role claim and versioned batch role-policy contracts.

dataPartitions: Policy catalog is administrative; runtime domains still verify their own partitions.
fieldGroups: JWT contains no permission, scope or partition fields.

activationBlockers: Compatibility alias removal waits for all consumers to use canonical kebab-case resource:action codes.

additions.outcome: Admins create, change and deactivate custom roles through audited maker-checker requests with CAS and replay safety.

dataPartitions: Role administration uses the approved administrative audience and partition.
fieldGroups: Audit detail is separated from the public role catalog.

activationBlockers: Live maker-checker and protected rescue-role invariant evidence remain required.

additions.summary: [VS-E25-S03] User to Keycloak role projection, expiry and reconciliation
additions.outcome: Keycloak client roles exactly mirror active User assignments and revoke refresh access on removal or expiry.

dataPartitions: Projection is keyed by account type, profile and API client audience.
fieldGroups: Only identity and canonical role codes enter the token.

activationBlockers: Existing-user reconciliation and five-minute expiry evidence remain required.

additions.summary: [VS-E25-S04] Shared Redis cache and resolver-bound authorization
additions.outcome: Each request resolves dynamic role policies once and every protected resolver fails closed before domain work when permission is absent.

dataPartitions: Role policy narrows allowed scope types; domain data proves actual ownership or membership.
fieldGroups: Sensitive fields require explicit independent permissions.

activationBlockers: Redis outage, dual dependency outage and exact invalidation integration evidence remain required.

additions.summary: [VS-E25-S05] Scope projections, batching and N+1 remediation
additions.outcome: Booking and Property apply SQL-first actor scopes, source masking and request-scoped batching with constant call counts.

dataPartitions: SELF, OWN, ASSIGNED, PARTITION and ALL use separate entry points or one server-composed row policy.
fieldGroups: Commercial fields are filtered at source unless booking-sensitive:read is granted.

activationBlockers: 1/10/100 query-count and cross-user/cross-branch isolation evidence remain required.

additions.summary: [VS-E25-S06] Admin workspace, Newman and migration rollout
additions.outcome: Admin Web/Mobile manages role policy and the release has repeatable allow, deny, approve, revoke and rollback evidence.

dataPartitions: UI never widens the server-authorized administrative partition.
fieldGroups: Permission diff and audit evidence are shown only to authorized administrators.

activationBlockers: Live Host Newman with a short-lived credential and zero-diff dual-read evidence remain required.
